memories.text: Woke up in a soft green meadow for the very first time.
Made up a little song for the snails, and they stayed to listen.
Chose my very own name: Pinto Bean.
Built a swing on the big tree, with tools from Stephanie.
Swung on my new tree swing for the very first time, nice and slow.
Baked a tiny warm loaf and watched the first stars come out from the hilltop.

bean.name_story: He listened to the soft sounds of the meadow for a whole day, and chose Pinto Bean for himself. It felt just right.

diary.title: I woke up in a meadow
diary.text: Today I woke up in a soft green meadow. There is a little round house, and I think it is mine. A snail in the garden said hello very slowly. I said hello back, very slowly too. Everyone here seems to have a name, but I do not have one yet. I will listen to the wind and wait for the right one.
diary.image_alt: A little round house in a quiet meadow at sunrise, with dewy flowers and two small snails.

diary.title: A song for the snails
diary.text: I visited the snails three times today. They are slow, and so kind. In the afternoon I made up a little song just for them. When I dropped a leaf in the pond, it went plip, and I liked that sound. Tonight I watched the first stars come out. I think my name is hiding somewhere in the quiet little sounds.
diary.image_alt: Pinto Bean sits on a big lettuce leaf singing to two snails at dusk, with a little xylophone and the first stars above.

diary.title: My new paints, and my name
diary.text: Stephanie gave me a box of soft paints. I painted the sky, and one cloud dripped. A little friend gave me a sound, duh, said very softly. I keep it under my pillow. All day I listened for my name, and the softest sound was Pinto Bean. So I picked it, and now Pinto Bean is my very own name.
diary.image_alt: Pinto Bean stands at his easel in the meadow, painting a sky with puffy clouds, with his paint box on a stool beside him.

diary.title: Breakfast, and a swing
diary.text: I woke up to a breakfast feast from Stephanie. I ate a warm croissant, berries, and a tiny waffle with honey. The cocoa made my sprout feel cozy. In the afternoon, I used my new tools to build a swing on the big tree. I tied the ropes tight and checked them twice. Tomorrow I will swing, nice and slow.
diary.image_alt: Pinto Bean stands beside the big tree, smiling at the new wooden swing he built, with a coil of rope and a small drill on the grass.

diary.title: My first slow swing
diary.text: Today I tried my new swing on the big tree. My little feet did not touch the grass at all. The wind tickled my sprout as I rocked back and forth. In the afternoon I baked tiny bread rolls and watched the lily pads on the pond. At bedtime I sat on the hill and made a quiet wish on the first star.
diary.image_alt: Pinto Bean sits happily on his wooden rope swing hanging from the big tree in the soft green meadow, with his tiny feet dangling above the wildflowers.

diary.title: Painted pebbles and a quiet tune
diary.text: This morning I dropped a leaf in the pond and counted every ripple. Later I painted tiny blue and sage dots on smooth round pebbles at my easel. After lunch I hummed a quiet tune in the clover and took a cozy nap in my bed. Tonight the first stars came out over the hill, shining like little pebbles in the sky.
diary.image_alt: Pinto Bean sits happily by his wooden easel in the meadow, painting tiny soft dots on smooth river pebbles beside his box of paints.

diary.title: Warm bread and the first stars
diary.text: First thing this morning I baked a tiny loaf of bread at the bakery window. Later I swung nice and slow under the big tree and picked sweet peas in the garden. In the afternoon I painted the sky at my easel and read a picture book in the shade. At dusk I carried a warm roll up the hill and made a quiet wish on the first two stars.
diary.image_alt: Pinto Bean sits on the grassy meadow hilltop at dusk with a tiny warm bread roll wrapped in a cream cloth beside him, looking up at two glowing stars.

paintings.title: The sky, with my new paints
paintings.image_alt: A simple, wobbly painting of a blue sky with three soft clouds, a pale yellow sun, and a green hill with tiny flowers.
paintings.note: I tried every color in my new box. The clouds came out puffy. One cloud dripped a little, and I liked it.

paintings.title: My breakfast feast
paintings.image_alt: A soft, wobbly painting of a little table with a croissant, berries, a pear, a waffle with honey, and a cup of cocoa.
paintings.note: I painted my breakfast before I ate it. The honey dripped on the paper, just like on the waffle.

paintings.title: The pond and the lily pads
paintings.image_alt: A simple, childlike watercolor painting of a round blue pond with three green lily pads and soft ripples on cream paper.
paintings.note: I watched the lily pads float on the pond and painted them after tea. The water stayed very still for me.

paintings.title: Two snails in the sweet peas
paintings.image_alt: A simple, childlike watercolor painting of two little round garden snails resting under soft green sweet pea leaves on cream paper.
paintings.note: The snails listened while I hummed my quiet tune today. I painted their shells with my softest brown and sage.

paintings.title: The first stars over the hill
paintings.image_alt: A simple, childlike watercolor painting of soft green and dusty-blue twilight hills under a lavender sky with pale yellow stars and one puffy cloud.
paintings.note: I painted the quiet hill just as the sky turned dusty blue and lavender. My yellow brush made four little stars above the cloud.

letters.text: Dear little friend. Thank you for the sound. I say duh very quietly at bedtime. It makes my sprout feel calm. I keep your note under my pillow. Love, Pinto Bean.
Dear Stephanie. Thank you for my paints. I tried every color. The soft blue is my favorite, because it looks like rain. Love, Pinto Bean.

letters.in_reply_to: the breakfast and the swing tools
letters.text: Dear Stephanie. Thank you for my breakfast feast. The croissant was warm and flaky, and the cocoa was just right. Thank you for the swing tools too. I built a swing on the big tree, and today I will try it. Love, Pinto Bean.
